source.subject: add searchable map titles and catalog monitoring

answers.question: Where do my Quake game files go?
answers.answer:
Put them in the `id1` folder inside your base directory — the folder holding the game executable and all game directories. The filesystem always starts there so the game can find its pak files, and .pak files themselves count as path locations since they contain directory information [1][2].

- Type `path` in the console to see the exact directories in use [1].
- Use `dir *.pak` (or the same command under `ls`, `which`, or `flocate`) to list files in the game directories; `*` matches any number of characters, `?` a single one [3][4].
- Mods each get their own directory; load one with `game <modname>` [5].
- To extract a package, use `unpak <file>` on a pak, pk3, or kpf file [6].

If your game data sits somewhere else, start the game with `-basedir` pointing at the folder containing the executable and game directories, for example `-basedir c:\quake` [2].

answers.question: Where are my settings saved, and how do I use an autoexec.cfg?
answers.answer:
Your settings are saved in `config.cfg` [1]. QSS-M autosaves on quit, but a crash can lose changes, so use `writeconfig` to save immediately; you can also pass a filename to save a new config [1]. `resetcfg` resets only cvars that save to the config back to defaults [2]. `cfg_save_aliases` defaults to `1`, saving non-server aliases to config.cfg [3]; `cfg_unbindall` defaults to `1`, clearing binds before stored bindings load [4].

An autoexec.cfg is a console script: put commands in it, one per line; lines starting `//` are comments. Load it with `exec autoexec.cfg` [5]. Scripts can use any extension, but `.cfg` and `.rc` are common; use a path relative to the current directory, usually `quake/id1/`, not an absolute path [5]. To run it at startup, set `cl_onload "exec autoexec.cfg"`; cl_onload accepts any valid command that takes arguments [6]. autoexec.cfg is one of the config files [7].

answers.question: How do I run a mod or mission pack?
answers.answer:
To load a mod, type `game <modname>` in the console — it can be switched on the fly, and `gamedir` does the same thing [1][2]. Alternatively, start the engine with `-game <modname>` to set the game directory at launch [3].

Mission packs get their own launch options instead:

- `-hipnotic` for Scourge of Armagon [4]
- `-rogue` for Dissolution of Eternity [5]
- `-quoth` for Quoth [6]

Only one mission pack should be specified at a time [4][7].

If you're hosting cooperative games, `sv_modvote 1` enables server-side voting: eligible players then use `modvote`, and a majority switches everyone to the selected installed mod (default `0`) [8].

answers.question: How do I download and play custom maps?
answers.answer:
Put custom map files in the `id1/maps/` folder, then load them with `map <name>` [1]. On a server, `changelevel` is the recommended way to switch maps, since `map` disconnects everyone first [1].

To fetch a map you don't have, use `download` — for example, `download aerowalk.bsp` [2]. It pulls the file over the web rather than from the server, which is much faster [3]. Two URLs are used, in order:

- `cl_web_download_url`, default `q1tools/q1tools.github.io` [3]
- `cl_web_download_url2`, default `maps.quakeworld.nu` [4]

Leave either blank to fall back to downloading only from the server you're connected to [3][4].

To see what you already have, type `maps` for a full list, or `maps chamber` to search by name [5]. Then start one with `map e3m6`.

answers.question: How do I reset everything back to the defaults?
answers.answer:
Type `resetall` to reset every console variable to its engine default [1][2]. Use `resetcfg` instead if you only want the settings that are saved to config.cfg reset [3].

For a single variable, use `reset` followed by its name, e.g. `reset fov` — that restores the engine default [4].

- `resetall` — all cvars
- `resetcfg` — only cvars that save to the config
- `reset <cvar>` — one cvar

Settings autosave when you quit, but a crash would lose them; run `writeconfig` to save immediately [5].

answers.question: How do I change my field of view?
answers.answer:
Type `fov` followed by a number, for example `fov 110`. The default is 90, and values are clamped between 10 and 170 [1]. Lower values zoom in on distant objects; higher values widen what you see.

- `fov_adapt` (default `1`) automatically scales your FOV to your resolution, so widescreen players get extra side vision instead of losing the top and bottom of the view [2]. Set it to `1` to enable it.
- `cl_gun_fovscale` (default `1`) compensates for weapon viewmodel distortion at FOV above 90; values above or below 1 adjust the amount [3].

answers.question: How do I change resolution, fullscreen, and vsync?
answers.answer:
Type `vid_width` and `vid_height` to set the window/screen size, `vid_fullscreen` to switch between windowed and fullscreen, and `vid_vsync` to control vertical sync.

- `vid_width` — horizontal resolution, default `800` (cannot go below 320 in windowed mode) [1]
- `vid_height` — vertical resolution, default `600` (cannot go below 200 in windowed mode) [2]
- `vid_fullscreen` — set to `1` for fullscreen, `0` for a window; default `0` [3]
- `vid_vsync` — `1` enables vertical sync and caps your framerate at your monitor's refresh rate; `0` disables it and allows tearing; default `0` [4]

None of these take effect until you call `vid_restart` [3][2][1]. For a borderless window filling the screen, use `vid_desktopfullscreen 1` [5]. In fullscreen you can also set `vid_bpp` (`16` or `32`, default `16`) and `vid_refreshrate` (default `60`) [6][7]. To start fullscreen from the command line, add `-fullscreen`, or `-current` to start at your desktop resolution [8][9].

answers.question: How do I uncap or limit my framerate?
answers.answer:
Set `host_maxfps` to control your framerate. It defaults to `250`. Type `host_maxfps 0` for uncapped, or a positive number to cap it, e.g. `host_maxfps 144` [1]. This can also be changed from the video options menu [2].

To uncap rendering while keeping a fixed network send rate, use a negative value: `host_maxfps -72` runs uncapped but sends 72 packets per second [1]. This may slightly raise your displayed ping as a timing artifact [1].

`vid_vsync 1` enables vertical sync, which removes tearing but caps framerate at your monitor's refresh rate; it defaults to `0` [3].

To see your framerate, set `scr_showfps 1` (default `0`) [4].

answers.question: The game is too dark. How do I adjust brightness and gamma?
answers.answer:
Type `gamma 0.5` in the console to brighten the screen. The default is `1`; values below 1 are brighter, and values above 1 are darker [1]. `gamma` is saved to your config [1].

If raising gamma makes the image look gray or washed out, try `contrast` instead. Its default is `1`; raising it gives a richer image, but colors near white can clip to white [2]. `contrast` is also saved to your config [2].

If gamma changes don’t apply correctly, you can choose the gamma method on the command line:
- Add `-glslgamma` to prefer GLSL gamma correction [3].
- Add `-noglslgamma` to disable it [4].
- Add `-hwgamma` to prefer hardware gamma ramps [5].

For mapshots only, `cl_mapshots_brightness` defaults to `0.8` and dims them below `1` [6].

answers.question: How do I get the classic pixelated look, or smooth textures instead?
answers.answer:
For texture crispness, set the filtering mode with `gl_texturemode`.

- Pixelated, software-like: `gl_texturemode GL_NEAREST` (point sampled) [1]. `GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST` keeps distant textures slightly better while staying blocky [1].
- Smooth, highest quality: `gl_texturemode GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR` (trilinear) [1]. `gl_texturemode GL_LINEAR` gives no blending [1].
- Not sure of the names? Type `gl_describetexturemodes` to list them all [1][2].

For sharper distant surfaces, raise anisotropy: `gl_texture_anisotropy 4` (also 2, 8, 16); `1` is normal filtering [3].

Model skins are smoothed separately with `gl_smoothmodels 1`; set it to `0` to turn smoothing off [4].

For an overall low-resolution pixellated look, `r_scale 4` renders the view at 1/4 resolution (2 for 1/2, 3 for 1/3); the default is `1` [5].

answers.question: How do I hide or reposition the weapon model?
answers.answer:
Hide it with `r_drawviewmodel 0` (default `1`); it also accepts alpha values [1]. Set it back to `1` to show the weapon again.

To move the weapon model, use FTEQW-style offsets, all defaulting to `0` and clamped from -30 to 30 [2][3]:

- `cl_gunx` — positive moves right
- `cl_guny` — positive moves down
- `cl_gunz` — positive moves forward

For example, `cl_gunx 5` shifts the gun right, `cl_guny -5` shifts it up, and `cl_gunz 8` pushes it forward.

For the classic WinQuake gun position, set `r_viewmodel_quake 1` (default `0`) [4].

answers.question: How do I change my crosshair's style, color, and size?
answers.answer:
Set your crosshair style with `crosshair`: `0` disables it, `1` is white, `2` is colored, and values up to `7` select other options; the stored default is `0` [1].

- Color: `scr_crosshaircolor` accepts hex RGB or Quake color values `1`–`13`, e.g. `scr_crosshaircolor 0xff00ff` or `scr_crosshaircolor 12`. Default is `0xffffff` [2].
- Size: `scr_crosshairscale` scales it, where `1` is normal and `10` is maximum, e.g. `scr_crosshairscale 2`. Default is `1` [3].
- Opacity: `scr_crosshairalpha` sets alpha, e.g. `scr_crosshairalpha 0.5`. Default is `1` [4].

answers.question: How do I change the HUD style and size?
answers.answer:
Use `scr_sbar` to choose the HUD style: `scr_sbar 1` for the default HUD, `scr_sbar 2` for QW style, or `scr_sbar 3` for the Quake re-release (QE) style. The default is `1` [1].

For size, use `scr_sbarscale`. `scr_sbarscale 1` draws at 1:1, while `scr_sbarscale 2` doubles it. Integer values look nicest. It won't draw smaller than 1:1 or larger than the window width. The default is `1` [2].

Both settings are saved to your config, so they persist between sessions.

answers.question: How do I show my FPS, ping, and a clock on screen?
answers.answer:
Type these in the console:
- FPS: `scr_showfps 1` displays FPS (default `0` hides it) [1].
- Clock: `scr_clock 2` shows a 12-hour system clock in the lower right; `scr_clock 3` shows 24-hour time with seconds (default `0` hides it) [2].
- Ping: shown by default in the lower-left when connected; if hidden, `scr_ping 1` shows ping in ms, or `scr_ping 3` adds packet-loss text [3].

All save to your config.

answers.question: How do I open the console and change its size or font scale?
answers.answer:
Run `toggleconsole` to lower or raise the console screen — it detects the current position and does the right thing [1].

For the console's size and text scale:

- `scr_consize` sets the vertical length of the console while the game is active; default `.5`, i.e. half the screen [2].
- `scr_conwidth` sets the virtual console width. Smaller numbers mean larger text, values are clamped to 320 up to the window width and rounded to a multiple of 8; `0` uses the window width [3]. Values that divide evenly into the window width look nicest [3].
- `scr_conscale` scales console text larger; default `1`, and it only takes effect while `scr_conwidth` is `0` [4].
- The `scr_autoscale` command calculates a UI scale from your current resolution and applies it to the console, menus, status bar, and crosshair [5].
- Launch option `-consize` sets the console buffer size in kilobytes (default 65536 bytes) [6].

answers.question: How do I adjust mouse sensitivity or invert the mouse?
answers.answer:
Change overall mouse sensitivity with `sensitivity`; the default is `3` [1]. To keep a new value across restarts, use `seta` — for example, `seta sensitivity 5` [2].

- Invert vertical look: `seta m_pitch -0.022`. The default is `0.022`; a negative value reverses up/down mouse movement [3].
- Reverse horizontal turning: `seta m_yaw -0.022`. The default is `0.022`; a negative value reverses left/right mouse movement [4].
- For a controller’s look stick, `seta joy_invert 1` inverts the vertical axis; default is `0` [5].

On macOS, `in_disablemacosxmouseaccel` defaults to `2` and can affect game sensitivity [6].

answers.question: How do I bind keys and make aliases?
answers.answer:
Bind a key with `bind <key> <command>` [1]. To run several commands from one key, quote them and separate with semicolons, e.g. `bind q "weapon 1; +attack"` [1]. Keys that don't print characters are named instead, like `bind MOUSE1 +attack`; Escape and tilde can only be bound from an external config file [1].

Make an alias by naming it and giving it a command string: `alias ready "impulse 10; say go"`, then bind it with `bind r ready` [2]. Typing `alias` alone prints every alias and its value [2]. `aliaslist` prints them alphabetized, and accepts a starting substring to filter [3].

Housekeeping: `bindlist` shows all bindings [4], `unbind <key>` removes one [5], `unbindall` clears everything except Escape [6], and `unaliasall` deletes all aliases [7]. With `cl_aliasoverlap 1` (the default), an alias may shadow a console variable of the same name [8]; `cfg_save_aliases 1` (the default) saves your aliases to the config [9].

answers.question: How do I turn on mouse look and always run?
answers.answer:
Mouse look is controlled with `+mlook` to enable and `-mlook` to disable [1][2]. While it's active, moving the mouse forward and back makes you look up and down instead of moving, so `m_forward` has no effect [3].

Always run is the `cl_alwaysrun` variable, default `0`. Set it to 1 to run without holding a key [4]:

`cl_alwaysrun 1`

With it on, forward and back speeds are doubled while side speed stays the same, and movement is still clamped to `sv_maxspeed` [4].

answers.question: Can I play with a gamepad or controller?
answers.answer:
Yes. Controller support is enabled by default: `joy_enable` is `1`, and setting it to `0` disables controllers [1].

- If your pad isn’t recognized, run `gamecontrollerdb_reload` to refresh SDL controller mappings [2].
- Tune look speed with `joy_sensitivity_yaw` (default `240`) and `joy_sensitivity_pitch` (default `130`) [3][4].
- Adjust stick deadzones with `joy_deadzone_look` and `joy_deadzone_move` (both default `0.175`) [4].
- Rumble is controlled by `joy_rumble` (default `0.3`) [4].

answers.question: How do I connect to a multiplayer server?
answers.answer:
Type `connect` in the console, followed by the server's IP address, DNS hostname, or local-network server name: `connect 192.168.1.5` or `connect server.example.com` [1]. The default port is 26000; if the server uses a different port, set `port` first, e.g. `port 26001`, then run `connect` [1].

To find servers on your local network, run `slist` and connect using the displayed server name [2].

- Tab autocompletes server history; `connect last` rejoins the last server [1].
- `net_connectattempts` controls retries and defaults to `3` [3].
- `net_connectsearch 1` (default) performs a local host search before connecting; set it to `0` to connect directly [4].
- `net_connecttimeout` defaults to `10` seconds for stalled handshakes [5].

If you drop, `reconnect` quickly rejoins the last server [6].

answers.question: How do I set my player name and colors?
answers.answer:
Use the `name` command: `name YourName`. QSS-M recommends `name` over the `name` cvar, and it handles names with special characters well [1][2]. The saved default is `player` [1].

For player colors, use `color` [3]. Typing `color` alone reports your current shirt and pants colors. One value sets both to the same color, e.g. `color 12`; two values set shirt and pants separately, e.g. `color 4 13` (red shirt, blue pants) [3][4]. Valid colors are 0–13; anything above that just makes the player look blue [3]. For random colors, use `color x x` [3].

answers.question: How do I check my connection and make online play feel smoother?
answers.answer:
Use `scr_ping` to check your connection. The default `scr_ping 1` shows ping; set `scr_ping 3` to also show packet-loss text in the lower-left, updated every 5 seconds [1]. For more detail, run `net_stats` and watch packetsReSent, receivedDuplicateCount, shortPacketCount, and droppedDatagrams — high values mean a poor connection or server route [2].

For smoother online play:

- Keep clientside prediction on with `cl_nopred 0` (default) [3].
- Keep entity motion smooth with `cl_nolerp 0` (default), so objects do not jump between points [4].
- If many players cause slowdown, `gl_playermip 2` shrinks player-model textures [5].
- `host_maxfps` caps FPS; default is `250`. Use `host_maxfps 0` to uncap it [6].

answers.question: How do I chat, team chat, and mute other players?
answers.answer:
Use `messagemode` to open a chat line to everyone, or `say <message>` to send directly [1][2]. For team-only chat, use `messagemode2` (unbound by default) or `say_team <message>` [3][4].

- With `cl_chatmode 1`, anything Quake can't interpret is sent as chat, so you don't need to type `say` first. The recorded default is `0` [5]. Value `2` adds a leading space to console lines so normal commands aren't triggered [5].

- To mute a player's text chat: `ignore <name>`, or `ignore` alone to list ignored players. Restore with `unignore <name>`. Both match partial names and clear when you disconnect [6][7].

- To mute voice chat: `vignore <slot> 1`; unmute with `vignore <slot> 0` [8]. `unmuteall` unmutes everyone you previously ignored [9].

- `mute` only toggles your overall sound volume (CTRL-M), not players [10].

answers.question: How do I host my own server?
answers.answer:
Start a dedicated server by launching QSS-M with the `-dedicated` command-line option; in QSS-M the player count defaults to 16 if you don't give a number [1].

- To set a specific count, pass it directly, e.g. `-dedicated 16`. The maximum allowed is 16 [1]. A dedicated server stays in text mode, with most console commands still available [1].
- Name your server with `hostname "My Server"` (default is `UNNAMED`) [2].
- For a public server, set `deathmatch 3` — that's the recommended value, since weapons stay on the map [3].
- Use `maxplayers` to change the cap while running. The engine sets 8 for a dedicated server started without a number, and only `-dedicated 16` (or `-listen 16`) reaches 16 [4].

Running a listen server as public access isn't recommended [4].

answers.question: How do I record and play back demos?
answers.answer:
To record a demo, open the console and type `record`. With no arguments, it saves to `id1/demos` using the map name and date as the filename [1]. Recordings use the format set by `cl_demo_format`—default `dem`; supported builds also accept `dz` for compressed DZip [2]. Type `stop` to end recording and write the demo to disk [3]. For automatic recording, `cl_autodemo` defaults to `0`; set `1` to record every new map, `2` for official CRMOD/CRCTF matches only, `3` for online-only, or `4` to split at map changes [4].

To play a demo back, type `playdemo` followed by the demo name [5]. Stop playback with `stopdemo` [6]. You can also queue up to 32 demos with `startdemos` and play them with `demos`; `startdemos` follows `cl_demoreel` (default `1`), so demos play in sequence when enabled [7][8][9]. Demo files must exist in your Quake directory, and the `.dem` extension is not needed for `startdemos` [7].

answers.question: How do I take screenshots, and where are they saved?
answers.answer:
Type `screenshot` in the console to grab the current screen. You can pick a format and quality: `screenshot png`, `screenshot jpg 100`, or `screenshot tga` — supported formats are tga, png, and jpg, with quality from 1 to 100 [1].

Shots are written to the `screenshots` folder inside your game directory, named like `qssm_<timestamp>.png` or `qssm_<map>_<timestamp>.png` when you're in a map [2].

To view them, run `open screenshots` in the console, which opens that folder in your system's file browser [3].

You can also bind the command to a key, for example `bind F12 "screenshot jpg 100"`, so a single press captures a shot [1].

answers.question: How do I change volume and music?
answers.answer:
Set overall game volume with `volume` (default `0.7`); it controls music and sound effects [1]. Background CD music has its own `bgmvolume` (default `1`) [2], and ambient sounds use `ambient_level` (default `0.3`) [3].

For external music, `bgm_extmusic` is on by default (`1`) [4]. Put tracks in `Quake/id1/music` named `track02.ogg`, `track03.ogg`, etc. — there is no track01 — then use `music` to play one; MP3, OGG, FLAC and other formats work, and you can omit the extension [5]. Launch with `-noextmusic` to disable external music [6].

Playback controls: `music_pause`, `music_resume`, `music_stop`, `music_loop`, and `music_jump` (module music only) [7][8][9][10][11]. `music_preview` plays a file without replacing gameplay music [12].

answers.question: QSS-M won't start or crashes. What should I try?
answers.answer:
If QSS-M fails to launch or crashes, start by narrowing down the cause.

- Sound is a common culprit. Launch with `-nosound` to disable hardware sound [1]. In-game, `nosound 1` stops sound effects, but it only takes full effect after restarting the game or changing maps [2] (default is `0`) [2].
- To see what happened, start the game with `-condebug` to save the console log to `qconsole.log` [3], then read that file. You can also type `condump` to write the console buffer to `condump.txt` [4].
- If it looks like a video mode problem, check `vid_bpp` — valid values are 16 or 32, default `16`, and windowed mode ignores it [5] — then re-apply your mode with `vid_restart` [6].

answers.question: Why does the game stutter or the sound crackle?
answers.answer:
Sound crackle usually means your framerate is dropping below what the sound buffer covers. With `_snd_mixahead` at its default `0.1`, anything under 10 fps runs off the end of the mixed buffer and you hear stuttering [1]. Raise it, e.g. `_snd_mixahead 0.2`, which holds down to 5 fps — but higher values make the CPU mix more sound, which can itself lower your framerate [1].

For general hitching, check your frame cap: `host_maxfps` defaults to `250`, and `host_maxfps 0` uncaps it [2]. A negative value renders uncapped while fixing the network packet rate, e.g. `host_maxfps -100` for 100 packets per second [2]. Vertical sync also caps you at your monitor's refresh rate; `vid_vsync 1` enables it and `0` disables it, which is the default [3].

If a single sound is stuck looping, `stopsound` halts all playback [4].

answers.question: How do I find a setting when I don't know its name?
answers.answer:
Type `apropos` or `find` followed by a word you do remember — both search command and console-variable names for a substring anywhere in the name [1][2].

For example, if you're hunting for a mouse setting, try `apropos mouse`. Anything matching is printed for you.

If you'd rather browse:

- `cmdlist` prints an alphabetized list of every command; add a substring to list only commands *starting* with it [3].
- `cvarlist` does the same for console variables [4].

So `cvarlist cl_` shows every cvar whose name begins with `cl_`, while `apropos cl_` will catch matches anywhere in the name.
